question.text: A compliance officer discovers that a promoter of a listed company, already holding 28% voting rights, has acquired an additional 4% within the current financial year (cumulative additional acquisition in the year is 4%, and no separate control trigger under Regulation 4 is present). What should the compliance officer advise?

answer.text: No mandatory open offer is triggered as the additional acquisition of 4% is within the 5% creeping acquisition limit
A mandatory open offer must be made immediately as any acquisition above 25% requires an open offer
The promoter must sell back the 4% acquired shares within 30 days
The promoter must make a public announcement for delisting

explanation.text: The Logic: Under Regulation 3(2) of the SEBI (SAST) Regulations, 2011, an acquirer who already holds 25% or more voting rights may further acquire up to 5% additional voting rights in any financial year without triggering a mandatory open offer. Since the cumulative additional acquisition in this financial year is 4% (below the 5% creeping-acquisition ceiling), no open offer is required. The Trap: Saying any acquisition above 25% needs an open offer ignores that the 25% threshold under Regulation 3(1) was already crossed at 28%; the live test now is Regulation 3(2)'s 5% creeping limit. The 30-day sell-back and delisting options have no basis in SAST for this fact pattern. Note: Explanation sentence repaired (previously broke at "Since 4% The Trap") and the stem now states the financial-year cumulative assumption and absence of any Regulation 4 control trigger explicitly.
